questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the lifecycle of a GitHub Copilot inline suggestion?

options.text: Model generates, gather context, proxy pre-filters, ghost text, post-processing
options.why: The model cannot generate before context is gathered, and post-processing happens before display.

options.text: Proxy pre-filters, gather context, post-processing, model generates, ghost text
options.why: Context must be gathered before the prompt reaches the proxy, and post-processing follows generation.

options.text: Gather context, model generates, build the prompt, ghost text, proxy pre-filters
options.why: The prompt is built and filtered before the model generates.

options.text: Gather context, build the prompt, proxy pre-filters, model generates, post-processing, ghost text
options.why: Correct. Context is gathered and the prompt built in the IDE, filtered by the proxy, generated by the model and post-processed before display.

questions.explanation: The order is context, prompt, proxy pre-filters, model, post-processing, then ghost text in the editor.

questions.question: A developer using Visual Studio Code on Windows sees an inline suggestion and wants to view the next alternative suggestion. Which key combination should the developer press?

options.text: Ctrl+I
options.why: Ctrl+I opens inline chat.

options.text: Alt+]
options.why: Correct. Alt+] shows the next suggestion, and Alt+[ shows the previous one.

options.text: Tab
options.why: Tab accepts the current suggestion.

options.text: Esc
options.why: Esc dismisses the suggestion.

questions.explanation: Alt+] and Alt+[ cycle through alternative inline suggestions (Option on macOS).

questions.question: Copilot suggests a method from an older version of a library. The current version renamed that method last month. Which limitation of large language models best explains this?

options.text: The public code filter is set to Allow.
options.why: The public code filter affects matches with public code, not library versions.

options.text: Content exclusions removed the library from context.
options.why: Exclusions apply to your repository paths, not to what the model learned.

options.text: Post-processing replaced the new method name.
options.why: Post-processing does not rewrite method names to older versions.

options.text: The model's training data has a knowledge cut-off.
options.why: Correct. Changes after the training cut-off may be unknown to the model.

questions.explanation: A knowledge cut-off means newer APIs and library changes may be missing or wrong in suggestions.

questions.question: Which three statements describe limitations of GitHub Copilot and large language models? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Suggestions are not executed or tested by the model before they are shown.
options.why: Correct. The model predicts code. It does not run or test it.

options.text: Suggestions are always free of security vulnerabilities after post-processing.
options.why: Post-processing catches some common patterns but does not guarantee secure code.

options.text: The model reads the entire repository for every inline suggestion.
options.why: The context window is limited, so only selected context is sent.

options.text: The same prompt can produce different output each time.
options.why: Correct. Model output is non-deterministic.

options.text: Suggestions can reference packages or APIs that do not exist.
options.why: Correct. This is called hallucination.

questions.explanation: LLM limits include non-determinism, hallucination, no execution, a knowledge cut-off, a limited context window and possible insecure code.

questions.question: A developer wants to accept only the first word of a multi-line inline suggestion in Visual Studio Code on Windows. What should the developer press?

options.text: Ctrl+Enter
options.why: Ctrl+Enter opens the completions panel with alternative suggestions.

options.text: Alt+[
options.why: Alt+[ shows the previous alternative suggestion.

options.text: Ctrl+Alt+I
options.why: Ctrl+Alt+I opens the Chat view.

options.text: Ctrl+Right Arrow
options.why: Correct. Ctrl+Right Arrow accepts the next word of the suggestion.

questions.explanation: Ctrl+Right Arrow accepts a suggestion one word at a time.
